summary: Richard Kieckhefer is a scholar in religious studies and history and archaeology. He studied at Saint Louis University (~1964–1968) and the University of Texas at Austin (~1968–1972). He took up a post at Northwestern University in 1975.

Richard King specializes in religious studies, philosophy, and Indology. He studied at Dalhousie, McGill, and Lancaster, and under Daniel Mariau. He held posts at the University of Stirling (~1992–1999), Vanderbilt University (~2002–2007), and the University of Glasgow (~2008–2011).

Richard M. Jaffe works in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. He held a position at North Carolina State University from ~1995 to 2000 before becoming a professor at Duke University around 2000.

Richard Mahoney works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned a Master of Arts at the University of Canterbury (~2000–2002) studying under Paul Harrison, Jens Braarvig, and Jonathan A. Silk, and later held a post there.

Richard Morris was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics who studied at Battersea Training College (~1852–1853). He served as a lecturer in English at King's College School (1871) and headmaster at the Royal Masonic School for Boys (1875–1891).

Richard N. Frye worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, history, and linguistics, studying at UIUC (~1935–1939) and Harvard (~1940–1946). He held posts at the OSS (~1942–1945), Harvard (~1948–1990), Hamburg (~1958–1959), and Frankfurt (~1959–1960).

Richard P. Boyle completed graduate work at the University of Washington (~1959–1964) and studied under traditional teacher Joshu Sasaki. He held teaching posts at the University of California, Los Angeles, and the University of New Mexico (~1970).

Richard P. Hayes, specializing in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology, earned a doctorate at the University of Toronto, studying under Shoryu Katsura, Bimal Krishna Matilal, and T. Venkatacharya. He held posts at Toronto, McGill, Leiden, and New Mexico.
Richard Peter Hottelet is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Narayan Hemandas Samtani and held a post at the University of Wisconsin-Madison.

Richard Pischel was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Breslau and under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler and Albrecht Weber. He held posts at Breslau, Kiel, Halle-Wittenberg, the Prussian Academy of Sciences, and Humboldt University of Berlin.
Richard Polenberg was a historian who studied at Columbia University (~1959–1964). He held a post at Cornell University from ~1966 to 2011.

Richard Rorty was a philosopher who studied at the University of Chicago (~1946–1952) and Yale University (~1952–1956). He held academic posts at Wellesley College (~1958–1961), Princeton University (~1961–1982), and Stanford University (~1998–2007).

Richard Salomon is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He has served as a professor at the University of Washington since ~1981 and was a visiting researcher at Soka University in 2007.
Richard Schmidt was an Indologist. He studied under Ernst Mehliß and completed studies at the University of Halle-Wittenberg between ~1885 and 1889.

Richard W. Lariviere is an Indologist who studied at Iowa (~1968–1972) and Pennsylvania (~1972–1976). He held posts at UT Austin (~1999–2006), Kansas (~2006–2009), Oregon (~2009–2011), and the Field Museum of Natural History (~2012–2020).
Richard Wilhelm was a Sinologist who studied at Eberhard-Ludwigs-Gymnasium (~1887–1891). He held academic posts at Peking University (~1922–1924) and Goethe University Frankfurt (~1924–1930).

Richard von Garbe was an Indologist and philosopher who studied under Rudolf von Roth at the University of Tübingen (1870–1879) and Bhagavata Acharya (~1885–1887). He held a chair at the University of Tübingen from 1895 to 1927.

Richard von Glahn is a scholar of Sinology and history. He has served as a professor at the University of California, Los Angeles since ~1987 and was a visiting fellow at the University of Tokyo from 1988 to 1989.

Riika J. Virtanen is a Tibetologist who conducted doctoral studies at the University of Helsinki (~2004–2014) supervised by Asko Parpola, Klaus Karttunen, and Hannu Riikonen, and also studied under Sangye Tandar Naga.
Rikizan Ishikawa was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at Komazawa University from ~1963 to 1973 and served there as Professor of Buddhist Studies from ~1978 to 1997.
